preamble: Deaspiration of the voiceless aspirated retroflex affricate [ʈʂʰ] to unaspirated [ʈʂ] keeps the place and manner of articulation and removes the delayed voice onset. A documented case is Lhasa (Central) Tibetan, which has a phonemic /ʈʂ/ : /ʈʂʰ/ contrast word-initially (/ʈʂʰaʔ/ 'blood') but neutralizes aspiration in plosives and affricates in the second syllable of disyllabic words. The cited acoustic example is velar; no retroflex-specific token is published in the source used here.

examples.to: [ʈʂ] in the second syllable of a disyllabic word
examples.note: Zhang (2025, citing Dawson 1980) states that aspirated plosives and affricates can deaspirate in the second syllable of a disyllabic word; the published example is [kʲi kɔʔ] < [kʲi] + [kʰɔʔ] 'Chinese hotpot'. The rule is stated for the whole aspirated series, which includes /ʈʂʰ/, but no retroflex compound is given.

sources: Zhang, Y. (2025). Central Tibetan (Lhasa). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 54, 788–810. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100324000033
